Clinical_Explanation: Memory impairment with functional_decline >= 2 should be interpreted as a dementia-stage prompt rather than MCI-like pattern.
Reference: Albert MS. Clinical_Explanation: Subjective memory complaint and memory-predominant MCI overlap; objective testing and functional assessment decide whether the MCI pattern is supported.
Reference: Albert MS. The diagnosis of mild cognitive impairment due to Alzheimer's disease: recommendations from the National Institute on Aging-Alzheimer's Association workgroups on diagnostic guidelines for Alzheimer's disease. Alzheimer's & Dementia. 2011;7(3):270-279. DOI: 10.1016/j.jalz.2011.03.008. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21514249/

Clinical_Explanation: Executive features alongside memory symptoms should trigger multidomain characterization rather than a pure memory-only interpretation.
Reference: Albert MS. The diagnosis of mild cognitive impairment due to Alzheimer's disease: recommendations from the National Institute on Aging-Alzheimer's Association workgroups on diagnostic guidelines for Alzheimer's disease. Alzheimer's & Dementia. 2011;7(3):270-279. DOI: 10.1016/j.jalz.2011.03.008. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21514249/

Clinical_Explanation: Language-predominant symptoms with less prominent memory impairment should prompt PPA/FTD evaluation before emphasizing typical AD.
Reference: Gorno-Tempini ML. Classification of primary progressive aphasia and its variants. Neurology. 2011;76(11):1006-1014. DOI: 10.1212/WNL.0b013e31821103e6. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21325651/

Clinical_Explanation: Dominant visuospatial or posterior cortical symptoms should route to atypical AD/PCA and visual/Lewy body differential assessment.
Reference: Crutch SJ. Consensus classification of posterior cortical atrophy. Alzheimer's & Dementia. 2017;13(8):870-884. DOI: 10.1016/j.jalz.2017.01.014. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28259709/

Clinical_Explanation: Basic ADL impairment indicates a more advanced functional stage than IADL-only dementia pattern.
Reference: Albert MS. The diagnosis of mild cognitive impairment due to Alzheimer's disease: recommendations from the National Institute on Aging-Alzheimer's Association workgroups on diagnostic guidelines for Alzheimer's disease. Alzheimer's & Dementia. 2011;7(3):270-279. DOI: 10.1016/j.jalz.2011.03.008. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21514249/

Clinical_Explanation: Early behavioral symptoms with executive dysfunction and limited memory impairment should prompt consideration of FTD rather than typical AD pattern.
Reference: Rascovsky K. Sensitivity of revised diagnostic criteria for the behavioural variant of frontotemporal dementia. Brain. 2011;134(Pt 9):2456-2477. DOI: 10.1093/brain/awr179. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21810890/

Clinical_Explanation: Visual hallucinations, delusions, or attention fluctuation should trigger Lewy body and delirium review even when multidomain impairment is present.
Reference: McKeith IG. Diagnosis and management of dementia with Lewy bodies: Fourth consensus report of the DLB Consortium. Neurology. 2017;89(1):88-100. DOI: 10.1212/WNL.0000000000004058. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28592453/

Clinical_Explanation: Attention-dominant or fluctuating symptoms reduce support for typical gradual AD until delirium, DLB, and medication effects are reviewed.
Reference: Inouye SK. Delirium in elderly people. Lancet. 2014;383(9920):911-922. DOI: 10.1016/S0140-6736(13)60688-1. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23992774/

Resolution_Strategy: Recommend vascular assessment when stepwise/focal features present
Clinical_Explanation: Executive dysfunction with stepwise decline or focal signs should prioritize vascular cognitive disorder evaluation.
Reference: Sachdev P. Diagnostic criteria for vascular cognitive disorders: a VASCOG statement. Alzheimer Disease and Associated Disorders. 2014;28(3):206-218. DOI: 10.1097/WAD.0000000000000034. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24632990/

Clinical_Explanation: Memory complaints with depressive or behavioral symptoms require mood and psychiatric review before AD-oriented staging.
Reference: Arvanitakis Z. Diagnosis and Management of Dementia: Review. JAMA. 2019;322(16):1589-1599. DOI: 10.1001/jama.2019.4782. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31638686/

Resolution_Strategy: Apply no-strong-pattern only if no higher-priority rule is met
Clinical_Explanation: The no-strong-pattern rule should never override memory, functional, multidomain, or differential red-flag rules.
